findings.locked_literal: critical temperature corresponds to the smallest of gamma_T and gamma_e
findings.reason: gamma_T and gamma_e are ordinates of different decreasing temperature curves; numeric comparison of the coefficients does not identify the earlier temperature. The predecessor ARSS method explicitly determines two temperatures and takes the smaller temperature.
findings.production_remediation: independently invert gamma_T and gamma_E on their own Appendix-B curves and use min(t_cr_T, t_cr_E)

findings.locked_literal: critical temperature by the smallest gamma_T obtained from Section 10 formulas
findings.reason: Each Section-10 gamma_T is a demand divided by ambient normative resistance. The Appendix-B gamma_T curve decreases with temperature. Therefore the largest required gamma_T reaches its limit first and corresponds to the smallest critical temperature.
findings.production_remediation: gamma_T_governing = max(applicable Section-10 gamma_T); then invert the gamma_T curve

findings.locked_literal: critical temperature by the smallest gamma_T obtained from Section 11 formulas
findings.reason: The same monotonic demand/capacity argument as Section 10 applies. Selecting the smaller required coefficient would select a later rather than earlier loss of capacity.
findings.production_remediation: gamma_T_governing = max(applicable Section-11 gamma_T); then invert the gamma_T curve

findings.source_location: Appendix B Table B.1 / Figures B.1-B.8
findings.production_remediation: exact Table-B.1 knots with linear interpolation only along published plotted segments; no extrapolation; gamma=1 maps to 250 C, upper end of unit plateau
high-strength group requires GOST 9651 / 600 C retention evidence; otherwise increased-strength coefficients are used
fire-resistant group fails closed unless the stated test/retention evidence is explicitly confirmed
